title: NWDAF Implementation: Addressing Ping-Pong Issues in 5G Networks for Abnormal Behaviour Analytics
authors: Quang-Vinh Tran; Tuan-Bach Phan; Quang-Diep Pham; Kieu-Ha Phung
venue: 2026 28th International Conference on Advanced Communications Technology (ICACT)
summary: Uses NWDAF abnormal-behaviour analytics with ML to predict handover ping-pong events before they happen and feeds the prediction into handover management.
method: ML prediction within NWDAF abnormal behaviour analytics
data_or_testbed: real subscriber data from Viettel's core network
key_result: Reports a substantial reduction in ping-pong handovers on operator data while keeping connectivity seamless.
limitation_or_critique: The loop acts on mobility parameters, not on NF selection or core restoration, and evaluation details are limited to one operator.

title: TeleGAN-Core: A BiLSTM Dual-Autoencoder GAN for 5G Core Anomaly Detection
authors: Ali Issa; Nahi Kandil; Nadir Hakem; Abdelwahab Hamou-Lhadj
venue: IEEE Access
summary: Proposes a one-class GAN whose generator and critic are BiLSTM autoencoders to detect anomalies in multivariate 5GC performance metrics grouped per NF and interface.
method: BiLSTM autoencoder GAN with fused reconstruction scores
data_or_testbed: production 5GC telemetry plus SWaT and WADI benchmarks
key_result: Reports stronger detection than compared methods on production 5GC metrics and two public benchmarks.
limitation_or_critique: Detection on NF/interface counters only; it does not use SCP-level message telemetry or localise and remediate faults.

title: Digital Twin-Assisted Handover Scheme for Mobile Networks Using Generative AI
authors: Lal Verda Cakir; Mehmet Ali Erturk; Mehmet Ozdem; Berk Canberk
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: A generative spatiotemporal twin produces counterfactual short-horizon trajectories for a candidate handover so that the AMF can approve or reject it before execution via standard signalling.
method: graph generative model with variational sampling (DT what-if generator)
key_result: Lowers handover failure rate and interruption time and improves latency, jitter, throughput and loss.
limitation_or_critique: Validates mobility actions only; core NF rerouting, failover or database actions and twin calibration against a live core are outside its scope.

title: Emulation Digital Twin Framework: Case Study on NGAP Attacks in 5G Control Plane
authors: Lal Verda Cakir; Arsen Duzgun; Kubra Duran; Mehmet Ozdem; Mehmet Ali Erturk; Berk Canberk
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Communications Workshops (ICC Workshops)
summary: Three-layer emulation twin (Containerlab, UERANSIM, extended Open5GS) that automates scenario generation and attack injection for iterative what-if evaluation of 5G control-plane countermeasures.
method: emulation-based digital twin with graph representation and orchestration layer
data_or_testbed: Open5GS + UERANSIM in Containerlab; NGAP DoS case study
key_result: Reduces experiment configuration effort by 81% in lines of code with little extra resource use.
limitation_or_critique: Offline emulation for security what-if studies; it is not synchronised to a live core and does not predict action outcomes at control-plane speed.

title: “Come Back Later”: Agentic Admission Pacing for 5G AMF Registration Storms
authors: Akihiro Nakao
venue: 2026 International Conference on Future and Intelligent Networking (FINE)
summary: Combines a deterministic AMF admission gate with an LLM agent that tunes the admission threshold and retry interval during registration storms in a real 5G core.
method: deterministic admission control + LLM agent at operator time scale
key_result: Converges 1.5-3.1 times faster than uncoordinated NAS retry on CPU-limited hosts and exposes a safety gap where retry intervals exceed the UE registration deadline.
limitation_or_critique: Studies storms caused by bursts of registrations, not NF failures or degraded back-ends, and does not provide a predictive model of UE outcomes.

title: A Machine Learning-Driven NWDAF Architecture For Intelligent 5G Core Networks
authors: Tsung-Fang Chen; Chien Chen; Jyh-Cheng Chen
venue: Proceedings of the 1st free5GC World Forum 2025
summary: Builds a 3GPP-style NWDAF with a separately deployable MTLF on free5GC that forecasts per-NF load and uses the forecasts to retune a charging-related URR threshold so that NFs avoid overload.
method: ML load forecasting in NWDAF (decoupled MTLF/AnLF) + rule-based actuation
data_or_testbed: free5GC with a custom UE testbed
key_result: The analytics-driven dynamic threshold prevented NF overload and improved stability compared with free5GC's static default configuration.
limitation_or_critique: The actuator is a charging parameter rather than NF selection, NRF/SCP routing or restoration, and the venue is a new short-paper forum.

title: NWDAF Implementation: Network Function Load Analytics in 5G Core Network
authors: Quang-Vinh Tran; Tuan-Bach Phan; Quang-Diep Pham
venue: 2025 16th International Conference on Information and Communication Technology Convergence (ICTC)
summary: Implements an NWDAF module dedicated to the NF load analytics ID, trained on operational data from an operator's 4G MME used as a stand-in for 5G NF behaviour.
method: NWDAF NF load analytics with ML on multivariate operator data
key_result: Shows that NF load analytics can be produced from real operator counters to support optimisation of network functions.
limitation_or_critique: Short paper; the analytics are not shown driving NF selection or any other actuator, and 4G MME data only approximates a 5G SBA core.

title: Design and Implementation of a Cost-Effective Failover Mechanism for Containerized UPF
authors: Kiem Nguyen Trung; Younghan Kim
venue: Electronics
summary: Detects containerised UPF failures quickly and restores the UPF either in the same Kubernetes cluster or in another cluster depending on resource availability and health, instead of keeping standby instances.
method: failure detection + intra/inter-cluster redeployment
key_result: Cuts UPF redeployment time by up to 37% and system cost by up to 50% compared with redundancy-based failover.
limitation_or_critique: User-plane only; control-plane state, subscriber-database replication and UE-procedure effects are not studied.

title: "Come Back Later": LLM-assisted Mitigation of 5G Core AMF Signaling Storms with Dynamic Retry Timer in SCTP
authors: Akihiro Nakao
venue: 2025 IEEE Globecom Workshops (GC Wkshps)
summary: Extends SCTP with a Come Back Later chunk so that an overloaded AMF, assisted by an LLM, can tell UEs when to retry before NAS processing starts, sidestepping static NAS retry timers.
method: transport-layer retry signalling with LLM assistance
key_result: Total registration time for 500 UEs fell from 35.7 s to 11.6 s, and to 10.6 s with pre-configured UPF tunnels.
limitation_or_critique: Mitigation mechanism rather than a predictive model; overload storms only, not NF or back-end failures, and it requires a non-standard SCTP extension.

title: Signaling Storm Mitigation by Geographically Distributed C-plane NF Placement and Routing
authors: Masayuki Kurata; Akio Ikami; Sohei Itahara; Masaki Suzuki
venue: 2024 IEEE 10th International Conference on Network Softwarization (NetSoft)
summary: Attributes signalling storms to inter-site link congestion and single-instance overload and proposes joint geo-distributed placement and per-UE routing of control-plane NF instances.
method: placement and routing algorithms using utilisation and context counts
key_result: Substantially cuts inter-site signalling and evens out NF instance utilisation compared with existing placements.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation only; failure-driven rerouting, database failover and UE-level timer effects are not evaluated.

title: 5GShield: HTTP/2 Anomaly Detection in 5G Service-Based Architecture
authors: Nathalie Wehbe; Hyame Assem Alameddine; Makan Pourzandi; Chadi Assi
venue: 2023 IFIP Networking Conference (IFIP Networking)
summary: Detects HTTP/2 stream-multiplexing denial-of-service attacks on the 5G SBA with an autoencoder over application-layer SBI features rather than flow statistics.
method: autoencoder anomaly detection on HTTP/2 SBI features
data_or_testbed: 5G core testbed with simulated HTTP/2 attacks
key_result: Reaches an F1-score of 0.992 versus 0.78 for a flow-based detector, showing the value of SBI application-layer telemetry.
limitation_or_critique: Security-only fault model; SBI traffic is captured as a sniffed feed rather than at an SCP, and no root-cause or remediation step follows.

title: Unsupervised Graph-Sequence Anomaly Detection for 5G Core Network Control Plane Traffic
authors: Min Wang; Peng Li; Zhang Cheng; Wenmao Liu; Lei Nie; Haizhou Bao; Qin Liu; Kai Zhang
venue: 2023 IEEE 29th International Conference on Parallel and Distributed Systems (ICPADS)
summary: Proposes GSAD, which models 5GC control-plane traffic as a directed NF-interaction graph and adds normalising flows over time to detect anomalies without labels.
method: graph modelling + temporal normalising flows (unsupervised)
key_result: Outperforms baseline detectors clearly across several injected scenarios on the testbed.
limitation_or_critique: Security-oriented scenarios on a single open-source testbed; detection only, with no localisation or link to SCP/NRF actions.

title: SENTINEL: Self Protecting 5G Core Control Plane from DDoS Attacks for High Availability Service
authors: Aditya Chilukuri; Shwetha Vittal; A Antony Franklin
venue: 2023 15th International Conference on COMmunication Systems & NETworkS (COMSNETS)
summary: Self-protecting 5GC control plane that combines a Hierarchical Temporal Memory detector with an XDP/eBPF slice aggregator to isolate users who mount DDoS attempts.
method: HTM anomaly detection + XDP/eBPF enforcement
key_result: Isolates suspected malicious users with about 86% sensitivity while keeping service available for legitimate users without extra resources.
limitation_or_critique: Availability is protected against attack load only; NF or database failures and cross-site failover are not considered.

title: Anomaly Detection using a Semi-Supervised Deep Learning Model on Open 5G Core Metrics during User-Equipment Registration
authors: Akash Gopikrishnan; Arun Prakash; Christian Hein; Klauss Mößner; Marius Corici; Thomas Magedanz
venue: 2023 IEEE Conference on Standards for Communications and Networking (CSCN)
summary: Trains an LSTM autoencoder on CPU and memory metrics of core NFs during UE registration to flag stress-related anomalies.
method: semi-supervised LSTM autoencoder
key_result: Exceeds 97% accuracy with few false positives.
limitation_or_critique: Resource-metric anomalies only; registration outcomes for UEs are not predicted and faults are synthetic.

title: Practice on fifth-generation core (5GC) network fault self-recovery based on a Digital Twin
authors: Yifeng Zheng; Huaming Kong; Na Wang; Mei Li; Xiaoyu Wang; Zhesheng Xia; Pei Wang; Chenhao Wang
venue: Digital Twin
summary: Builds a digital twin of a 5GC (equipment, links and services) and uses its topology and simulation capabilities for fault propagation reasoning, disaster-recovery analysis and closed-loop self-recovery.
method: data-governance-based twin model + topology reasoning in a perceive-analyse-decide-execute loop
key_result: Reports fault detection within 1 minute, delimitation within 20 minutes and recovery within 5 minutes.
limitation_or_critique: Minute-scale practice report in an open-peer-review journal; twin fidelity and the predicted effect of recovery actions are not quantified.

title: Measuring What Matters: Increasing the Observability of Signalling Traffic in the 5G Core
authors: Simon Raffeck; Stanislav Lange; Andra Lutu; Tobias Hossfeld; Stefan Geissler
venue: 2026 IEEE 12th International Conference on Network Softwarization (NetSoft)
summary: Proposes a measurement method that extracts per-UE signalling information inside individual 5GC NFs and uses it to study attach-procedure performance and AMF stability in Open5GS under increasing load.
method: instrumentation-based measurement methodology
key_result: Provides per-UE, per-NF visibility of signalling and characterises how attach performance and the AMF behave under heavy load.
limitation_or_critique: Measurement study without a predictive model, fault injection or remediation; results are tied to one open-source core.

title: LLM-Guided Digital Twin for Network Experimentation: Fidelity, Robustness, and Optimization
authors: Rawlings Ntassah; Ayub Shah; Fabrizio Granelli
venue: ICC 2026 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
summary: Combines an LLM that generates scenarios, a random-forest KPI surrogate that filters them, and an ns-3 twin that validates the most promising ones in a feedback loop.
method: LLM scenario generation + random-forest surrogate + ns-3 twin
data_or_testbed: ns-3 simulations of transport-protocol and queue combinations
key_result: The surrogate predicts twin KPIs with R2 near 0.99 and the twin reproduces baseline KPIs consistently across batches.
limitation_or_critique: Fidelity is reported as repeatability and surrogate-to-twin agreement, not twin-to-real-network accuracy, and the setting is IP transport rather than a core.

title: Can AI Remediate Backend Failures Safely? GuardedAct with Blast-Radius-Aware Sandboxing
authors: Wanrong Cai; Tianyu Yu; Shaorui Pi; Xiaoxuan Sun; Wenrui Ma
venue: arXiv preprint
summary: Places a twin sandbox between an LLM that proposes ranked remediation actions and production, simulating each action's blast radius and auto-executing only low-risk ones.
method: LLM action generation + lightweight digital-twin sandbox + rollback-confidence gate
data_or_testbed: DeathStarBench social-network app with five injected faults
key_result: Recovers 87.4% of faults and cuts collateral damage from 25.6% to 5.2% versus direct LLM execution at about 8 s extra recovery time.
limitation_or_critique: Microservice benchmark rather than a telecom core; the sandbox models blast radius, not whether the action actually removes the cause.

title: AstroTimer: Rethinking Non-Access Stratum Timers in LEO Constellations
authors: Arshiya Rezaie Hezaveh; Peng Hu
venue: ICC 2026 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
summary: Derives a closed-form model to size NAS watchdog and back-off timers for 5G registration over LEO satellites from link variability, processing delays and NF placement.
method: closed-form timer model + simulation
key_result: Reduces registration time, retry frequency and UE energy compared with 3GPP default timers while avoiding signalling overload.
limitation_or_critique: Targets propagation-driven timer mismatch in NTN rather than core NF faults, and is evaluated in simulation only.
standards_link: TS 24.501 (NAS timers incl. T3510); TS 23.501 NTN

title: Location-Aware NAS Timer Optimization in NTN-TN Integrated Networks
authors: Cheng Liu; Peng Hu
venue: arXiv preprint
summary: Sets UE-specific NAS timers in integrated satellite-terrestrial networks by modelling path delay from link geometry and hop count and endpoint delay from expected AMF queueing and path reliability.
method: per-UE delay model + timer optimisation, simulation
key_result: Lowers registration latency, UE energy and avoidable registration attempts relative to fixed and global timers.
limitation_or_critique: Preprint; AMF queueing enters as an expected exposure, and core NF failures or failover transients are not modelled.

title: 5G-STREAM: Service Mesh Tailored for Reliable, Efficient and Authorized Microservices in the Cloud
authors: Tolga O. Atalay; Alireza Famili; Sudip Maitra; Dragoslav Stojadinovic; Angelos Stavrou; Haining Wang
venue: 2025 55th Annual IEEE/IFIP International Conference on Dependable Systems and Networks (DSN)
summary: Builds a 5GC-specific service mesh that learns the topology of service chains across cloud tiers and configures paths to reduce NRF discovery and authorisation signalling.
method: topology-aware service-mesh path configuration
key_result: Halves inter-VNF-to-NRF latency per transaction in core service chains at a cost of about 0.1 USD per hour per VNF.
limitation_or_critique: Targets signalling overhead and latency; the mesh is not used as a telemetry source for analytics or fault diagnosis.

title: Predictive Disaster Recovery for Multi-Redundant Operations and Maintenance 5G Network Systems
authors: Charles F. Santos; Augusto V. Neto; Ramon R. Fontes; Roger Immich; Vicente Sousa; Helber W. Da Silva
venue: 2025 International Wireless Communications and Mobile Computing (IWCMC)
summary: ML-driven disaster recovery that predicts failures of 5G operations-and-maintenance systems from KPIs and picks the backup instance among several redundant candidates using migration-cost estimates.
method: ML failure prediction + cost-based backup selection
key_result: Maintains service continuity better than baseline switchover logic in the proof of concept.
limitation_or_critique: Protects OAM systems rather than core NFs or subscriber databases, and the evaluation is a small proof of concept.

title: NFVAgent: A Retrieval-Augmented LLM Agent for Resilient NFV Failure Recovery
authors: Yeunjin Woo; Honguk Woo
venue: 2025 21st International Conference on Network and Service Management (CNSM)
summary: Uses a retrieval-augmented LLM agent whose knowledge base is updated from testbed and deployment experience to choose recovery actions for NFV failures.
method: RAG-based LLM agent for recovery-action generation
data_or_testbed: alarm dataset of over 500 failure events across NFV environments
key_result: Reaches up to 99.8% recovery accuracy, about 38 points above policy-based methods in multi-tenant settings.
limitation_or_critique: Accuracy is measured against labelled recovery actions; the effect of an action is not predicted or tested before execution, and 5GC procedures are not modelled.

title: Toward Trustworthy Digital Twins in AI Agent-based Wireless Network Optimization: Challenges, Solutions, and Opportunities
authors: Zhenyu Tao; Wei Xu; Xiaohu You
venue: arXiv preprint
summary: Argues that twins used to train or test network agents must be judged on the decision process the agent sees, and proposes a task-centric twin evaluation framework instead of model-level similarity.
method: task-centric (MDP-based) twin evaluation framework
data_or_testbed: real-world wireless network testbed case study
key_result: The framework pre-filters candidate twins and reduces training and testing cost without hurting deployed performance.
limitation_or_critique: Wireless/RAN optimisation focus and preprint status; core control-plane twins and failure actions are not covered.

title: Design and Evaluation of a Network Digital Twin Framework for 5G/6G Architectures
authors: Ioannis Vasalos; Maria Christopoulou; Averkios Vasalos; Michail Alexandros Kourtis; Nikos Dimitriou; George Xylouris
venue: 2025 21st International Conference on Distributed Computing in Smart Systems and the Internet of Things (DCOSS-IoT)
summary: Presents an NDT framework for B5G/6G that generates the twin model, mirrors topology and synchronises with a physical 5G testbed to support AI-native functions.
method: NDT framework with model generation and synchronisation
key_result: Demonstrates end-to-end deployment of the twin integrated with a real 5G testbed.
limitation_or_critique: The abstract reports no quantitative fidelity or what-if accuracy for core procedures.

title: Open-Source 5G Digital Twin: Virtualizing Core and RAN for Network Replication
authors: Cristhian J. Rodrigues D.S; Izan Mateos; Jose A. Lazaro; Joan Anguera; Anna Umbert
venue: 2025 25th Anniversary International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
summary: Proposes a methodology for twinning a multi-campus 5G network with open-source cores (Open5GS, free5GC, OAI) and RAN, including bidirectional synchronisation, and compares the cores for this use.
method: emulation-based twin with open-source NFs
key_result: Provides benchmarks and implementation guidelines for open-source high-fidelity network replicas.
limitation_or_critique: Largely a proposed methodology; fidelity is asserted rather than measured against the physical network.

title: Orchestrating Cross-Layer Anomaly Detection and Mitigation to Address Gray Failures in Large-Scale Cloud Infrastructure
authors: Ze Li; Chang Lou; Vignatha Yenugutala; Vivek Ramamurthy; Eion Blanchard; Minghua Ma; Murali Chintalapati
venue: 2025 IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Cloud Intelligence & AIOps (AIOps)
summary: Panacea correlates host, VM and application signals to detect gray failures and orchestrates fine-grained, safe mitigation across layers in production cloud infrastructure.
method: cross-layer detection + orchestrated multi-level mitigation
data_or_testbed: production deployment at millions of hosts
key_result: Deployed in production and addresses anomalies that host-only reboots leave to manual work.
limitation_or_critique: Cloud-host setting; mitigation choice is policy-driven and its effect is not predicted per candidate action.

title: Service Failure Detection via Connection Retry Analysis of User Traffic
authors: Naoki Hayashi; Fumio Katayama; Naoki Tateishi; Osamu Okino; Mitsuho Tahara
venue: NOMS 2025-2025 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Detects silent service failures in a telecom network by spotting simultaneous surges of several control signals that users send while trying to re-establish connections.
method: detection of correlated control-signal surges
data_or_testbed: real traffic data from a telecom operator
key_result: Finds failures that volume-based methods miss while keeping false alarms low.
limitation_or_critique: Uses retries as a symptom for detection rather than predicting them from a procedure model, and is not specific to 5GC NFs.

title: Analyzing Metastable Failures
authors: Rebecca Isaacs; Peter Alvaro; Rupak Majumdar; Kiran-Kumar Muniswamy-Reddy; Mahmoud Salamati; Sadegh Soudjani
venue: Proceedings of the Workshop on Hot Topics in Operating Systems
summary: Proposes an ensemble of queueing models, discrete-event simulation and emulation to find the conditions under which a service is vulnerable to retry-driven metastable collapse.
method: queueing models + DES + service emulation
key_result: Shows how an engineer can iteratively build a performance model that predicts metastable vulnerability.
limitation_or_critique: Workshop paper on generic services; no cellular procedures or NAS timers.

title: Modeling and Analysis of mMTC Traffic in 5G Core Networks
authors: Endri Goshi; Fidan Mehmeti; Thomas F. La Porta; Wolfgang Kellerer
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Derives the inter-arrival distribution of aggregated mMTC traffic at the base station and at the core network and validates it with traces and testbed measurements.
method: analytical traffic modelling + validation
key_result: The arrival process at the core is shown to be Poisson, but convergence needs very many packets as users and base stations grow.
limitation_or_critique: Arrival modelling under normal operation; procedure failures and retry behaviour are not modelled.

title: Performance Evaluation of 5G Core Network Control-Plane Using Open5GS and Kubernetes
authors: Sooraj Subramanian M S; Madhan Raj Kanagarathinam; Krishna M. Sivalingam
venue: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
summary: Evaluates latency, throughput and resource use of an Open5GS control plane on Kubernetes with over 50,000 emulated UEs and releases the packet traces.
method: large-scale experimental evaluation
data_or_testbed: Open5GS on Kubernetes, more than 50,000 emulated UEs
key_result: Identifies which NFs to prioritise for scaling and provides public control-plane traces.
limitation_or_critique: Normal-load measurements only; failure scenarios and UE timer outcomes are not covered.

title: Resource-Aware Service Prioritization in a Slice-Supportive 5G Core Control Plane for Improved Resilience and Sustenance
authors: Supriya Kumari; Shwetha Vittal; Antony Franklin A
venue: 2024 IEEE 21st Consumer Communications & Networking Conference (CCNC)
summary: Monitors 5GC NFs proactively and uses a max-flow formulation to route and prioritise critical slice requests when NFs fail, overload or congest.
method: max-flow (Ford-Fulkerson) based assessment and scheduling
key_result: Serves 20% more requests in a native core and 33-47% more mMTC/URLLC slice requests at peak.
limitation_or_critique: Single-site, no learning component, and no evaluation of database failover or UE-visible procedure outcomes.

title: Resilient User Plane Traffic Redirection in Cellular Networks
authors: Lisa Wernet; Laura-Marie Spang; Fridolin Siegmund; Tobias Meuser
venue: 2024 IEEE Conference on Network Function Virtualization and Software Defined Networks (NFV-SDN)
summary: Mirrors UPF session state proactively to a second instance and redirects user-plane traffic after a UPF failure, transparently to gNBs and devices.
method: proactive session mirroring and traffic redirection
key_result: Shows feasible, scalable recovery with shorter user-plane recovery times than standard restoration.
limitation_or_critique: User-plane only and single-site; no learning component and no control-plane or database failover.

title: A First Look at the Impact of Measurement on Orchestrating Digital Twin Network
authors: Weichen Tao; Leonardo Linguaglossa
venue: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Cloud Networking (CloudNet)
summary: Classifies network measurement schemes and evaluates how the act of measuring perturbs the system, arguing that this observer effect limits the accuracy of a network digital twin.
method: review and classification of measurement schemes + experiments
key_result: Quantifies performance degradation caused by measurement and explains its causes for twin construction.
limitation_or_critique: Simple generic network; no core-network twin or end-to-end twin fidelity metric.

title: Evaluation of UE Registration Performance in Open-Source 5G Core Networks
authors: Peng-Yu Chen; Chin-Ya Huang
venue: 2024 IEEE VTS Asia Pacific Wireless Communications Symposium (APWCS)
summary: Measures UE registration behaviour of free5GC, Open5GS and OAI at three scales and under many duplicate registration requests hitting the AMF.
method: experimental measurement
key_result: Reveals scalability and duplicate-request handling differences among the three open-source cores.
limitation_or_critique: Descriptive measurements without a model or fault injection beyond duplicate requests.

title: High-Fidelity Cellular Network Control-Plane Traffic Generation without Domain Knowledge
authors: Z. Jonny Kong; Nathan Hu; Y. Charlie Hu; Jiayi Meng; Yaron Koral
venue: Proceedings of the 2024 ACM on Internet Measurement Conference
summary: CPT-GPT, a transformer that synthesises per-UE control-plane event streams without hand-built domain models while respecting stateful semantics.
method: transformer generative model
key_result: Matches the fidelity of the state-machine generator and cuts streams violating stateful semantics by two orders of magnitude versus a GAN.
limitation_or_critique: Generates normal-condition traffic; behaviour under core failures and retries is not addressed.

title: MSF-Model: Queuing-Based Analysis and Prediction of Metastable Failures in Replicated Storage Systems
authors: Farzad Habibi; Tania Lorido-Botran; Ahmad Showail; Daniel C. Sturman; Faisal Nawab
venue: 2024 43rd International Symposium on Reliable Distributed Systems (SRDS)
summary: Develops a queueing model that characterises and predicts metastable failures, where retries and load sustain a collapse, in consensus-based replicated storage.
method: queueing-based analytical model validated by experiments
key_result: Predicts metastable failures with high accuracy compared with real experiments.
limitation_or_critique: Generic storage systems; it is transferable to retry storms after core database failover but not applied to telecom procedures.

title: Recommending Root-Cause and Mitigation Steps for Cloud Incidents using Large Language Models
authors: Toufique Ahmed; Supriyo Ghosh; Chetan Bansal; Thomas Zimmermann; Xuchao Zhang; Saravan Rajmohan
venue: 2023 IEEE/ACM 45th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
summary: Large-scale study at Microsoft of whether GPT-3.x models, zero-shot or fine-tuned, can recommend root causes and mitigation steps for production cloud incidents.
method: LLM fine-tuning and evaluation with lexical/semantic metrics and human review
key_result: Fine-tuned models produce useful root-cause and mitigation recommendations according to metrics and incident owners.
limitation_or_critique: Recommendations are text and are not checked for effectiveness before being applied; no network-core semantics.

title: Modeling and Generating Control-Plane Traffic for Cellular Networks
authors: Jiayi Meng; Jingqi Huang; Y. Charlie Hu; Yaron Koral; Xiaojun Lin; Muhammad Shahbaz; Abhigyan Sharma
venue: Proceedings of the 2023 ACM on Internet Measurement Conference
summary: Proposes a two-level hierarchical state-machine model of per-UE control-plane events, including inter-arrival and sojourn times, and an open-source generator adaptable from LTE to 5G.
method: hierarchical state-machine traffic model
key_result: Generates large realistic control-plane traces validated against real data.
limitation_or_critique: Models normal UE event behaviour; core faults, NAS timer expiries and retry dynamics under failure are not modelled.

title: Proactive and AoI-Aware Failure Recovery for Stateful NFV-Enabled Zero-Touch 6G Networks: Model-Free DRL Approach
authors: Amirhossein Shaghaghi; Abolfazl Zakeri; Nader Mokari; Mohammad Reza Javan; Mohammad Behdadfar; Eduard A. Jorswieck
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Formulates zero-touch proactive failure recovery of stateful VNFs as a cost-minimisation problem and solves it with SAC and PPO agents trained on an impending-failure model, using age of information to schedule monitoring.
method: model-free DRL (SAC, PPO) with LSTM layers; age-of-information monitoring
key_result: Provides design insights showing that hybrid LSTM-DRL agents capture impending-failure dynamics for proactive recovery.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-only and generic NFV; it does not address 5GC NF sets, restoration procedures or UE procedure impact.

title: Petri Net-Based Model for 5G and Beyond Networks Resilience Evaluation
authors: Rui Li; Bertr Decocq; Anne Barros; Yiping Fang; Zhiguo Zeng
venue: 2022 25th Conference on Innovation in Clouds, Internet and Networks (ICIN)
summary: Extends Petri nets to model physical and virtual infrastructure, network services and their dependencies for resilience and availability assessment of NFV-based 5G networks.
method: extended Petri net + simulation
key_result: Simulated availability estimates show the model can support resilience assessment of complex telecom systems.
limitation_or_critique: Infrastructure-level availability model; UE procedures and timer-driven outcomes are not represented.

title: Adaptive and Latency-aware Load Balancing for Control Plane Traffic in the 4G/5G Core
authors: Van-Giang Nguyen; Karl-Johan Grinnemo; Javid Taheri; Anna Brunstrom
venue: 2021 Joint European Conference on Networks and Communications & 6G Summit (EuCNC/6G Summit)
summary: Designs three adaptive load-balancing policies for a distributed virtual MME that use instance load, request completion time and queue length instead of round-robin or hashing.
method: adaptive load-balancing algorithms (load-, latency- and queue-aware)
key_result: The latency-aware policy cut signalling completion time by up to five times when balancer-to-instance delays differ strongly.
limitation_or_critique: Applies to an MME pool in 4G/NSA cores rather than SBA NF selection via NRF/SCP, and uses live measurements rather than standard analytics.
standards_link: TS 23.401 (MME pool); relevant to TS 29.510 NF selection policy

title: A composition framework for change management
authors: Ajay Mahimkar; Carlos Eduardo de Andrade; Rakesh Sinha; Giritharan Rana
venue: Proceedings of the 2021 ACM SIGCOMM 2021 Conference
summary: CORNET breaks operator network changes into reusable blocks, composes them into workflows, optimises change plans and verifies change impact, using data from 4G/5G and virtualised services at a large provider.
method: modular change workflows + plan optimisation + statistical impact verification
data_or_testbed: AT&T 4G/5G and cloud VNF data; VNF testbed
key_result: Has been used in production at a large service provider for three years.
limitation_or_critique: Impact is verified after deployment on real elements rather than predicted for a candidate remediation, and core NF failover is not a use case.

title: ECHO: A Reliable Distributed Cellular Core Network for Hyper-scale Public Clouds
authors: Binh Nguyen; Tian Zhang; Bozidar Radunovic; Ryan Stutsman; Thomas Karagiannis; Jakub Kocur; Jacobus Van der Merwe
venue: Proceedings of the 24th Annual International Conference on Mobile Computing and Networking
summary: Presents ECHO, a cellular core architecture designed for public-cloud deployment where component availability is much lower than on telco hardware, treating the core as a distributed state machine.
method: distributed, replicated core state-machine design
data_or_testbed: implementation on a public cloud platform
key_result: Analysis indicates higher availability than existing telco core solutions.
limitation_or_critique: Pre-2020 LTE-era design without AI; it is foundational for cloud-scale core reliability but not evaluated against 5G SBA restoration.
